source.citation: Photographic face-texture processing of retained, individually credited portraits and labelled stand-ins (26 November 2026). Original archive citations remain in their source records.
what_it_does_not_supply: A new historical reading, an unlabelled identity substitution, colour evidence from monochrome photographs, or unseen profile measurements.
what_it_supplies: Cabinet-card portrait of Anna Åkerman, Uddevalla: public domain; Bohusläns museum marks the image Public Domain Mark 1.0 (K-samsök mediaLicense 'pdmark'; Europeana edmRights PDM 1.0). A studio photograph of about 1890-1895; under Swedish law the protection of a simple photographic picture made before 1969 has expired.

Chicago Sunday Tribune, 3 March 1907, Part 7/Special Features, p. 4, How…: public domain; Published in the United States in 1907; copyright term expired. MSU identifies the publication date and provides a direct scan of the printed page.

Photograph of Frances Macbeth Glessner standing in a conservatory among potted…: public domain; The museum's record marks the image 'No Copyright - United States'; a photograph made in 1892 is out of copyright in the United States. Credit: Chicago History Museum, ICHi-061818.

Photograph of Martha L. (Mattie) Williamson, head and shoulders, captioned…: public domain; The post gives no credit line or rights statement for this image. The photograph was made in the 1890s by its caption; a photograph made before 1906 is out of copyright in the United States whether or not it was published (published before 1931, or unpublished and more than 120 years old with no named author). The museum's digitisation adds no new copyright under US law for a faithful copy. Credit as: Glessner House Museum. The museum may hold the original and could be asked for a better scan.

Harris & Ewing, Mrs. George M. Pullman, half-length portrait, seated, facing…: public domain; US copyright registration H105262 in 1908; term expired. Wikimedia Commons reproduces the LOC catalogue and identifies the image as public domain.

[House maid ironing a lace doily with GE electric iron]: no known restrictions; The Library of Congress states 'No known restrictions on publication.' A photograph copyrighted in 1908 is in the public domain in the United States.

'Nordström, Kusk, Vänersborg' ('Nordström, coachman, Vänersborg'): public domain; K-samsök (the Swedish heritage aggregator, record built 2026-11) gives the image licence as Public Domain Mark 1.0 ('pdmark'). Europeana's older copy of the record gives CC BY-SA 4.0 instead; the museum's current feed is taken as authoritative here, and the conflict is recorded. A studio photograph made in 1903 is out of protection under Swedish law (simple photographic pictures made before 1969).

'Kusken Kalén' ('Kalén the coachman'): public domain; Västmanlands läns museum marks the image Public Domain Mark 1.0 (K-samsök mediaLicense 'pdmark'; Europeana edmRights PDM 1.0). If the negative is from the 1920s rather than earlier, the museum's mark is still the stated status; under Swedish law a simple photographic picture made before 1969 is out of protection.
